summary: Authentication module contains critical SQL injection, unhandled null references, plaintext password verification, and hardcoded secrets.

findings.title: SQL Injection in User Lookup
findings.body: The username input is directly concatenated into the SQL query in findUser without sanitization or parameterization, allowing arbitrary SQL injection attacks.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g., db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])).

findings.title: Unhandled Null Pointer on Non-Existent User
findings.body: When findUser returns null or undefined for an unknown user, accessing user.password in login throws an unhandled TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Add a null check before accessing user properties (e.g., if (!user || !user.password) return null;).

findings.title: Plaintext Password Comparison
findings.body: Passwords are verified using plaintext loose equality (==) rather than comparing salted cryptographic hashes with constant-time equality checks.
findings.recommendation: Use a secure password hashing library like bcrypt or argon2 to verify password hashes.

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret
findings.body: The JWT signing secret is hardcoded in source code, which risks credential exposure and allows unauthorized token generation if the codebase is leaked.
findings.recommendation: Retrieve the JWT secret from environment variables (e.g., process.env.JWT_SECRET) or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Uncaught SyntaxError in Session Parsing
findings.body: JSON.parse(raw) throws an unhandled SyntaxError when provided malformed input, and will throw a TypeError accessing userId if raw parses to null.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch block and verify the parsed result is a non-null object before accessing userId.

samples.summary: The authentication module contains a critical SQL injection vulnerability, hardcoded secrets, missing null checks on user lookup, and missing dependencies.

findings.title: SQL injection via string concatenation in findUser
findings.body: In findUser(), the username parameter is directly concatenated into the SQL query string without sanitization or parameterization. An attacker can supply SQL payloads to bypass authentication or extract/modify database records.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements supported by your database client (e.g., db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])).

findings.title: Uncaught TypeError on user lookup failure in login
findings.body: In login(), findUser(username) is called and user.password is accessed directly without verifying if user exists. If no matching user is returned (null/undefined), accessing user.password throws an unhandled TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Check that user is non-null before accessing user.password (e.g., if (user && user.password === password)).

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret key
findings.body: The secret key used to sign JWT tokens is hardcoded as a plain string in source code. Anyone with access to the codebase can sign valid JWTs and impersonate arbitrary users.
findings.recommendation: Load the JWT secret from an environment variable (e.g., process.env.JWT_SECRET) and throw an error at startup if it is not configured.

findings.title: Missing local module './db' and undeclared dependencies
findings.body: The file requires './db' which does not exist in the repository, and imports 'jsonwebtoken' without a package.json manifest defining the dependency, leading to MODULE_NOT_FOUND runtime errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement the missing db module at src/db.js and create a package.json file declaring jsonwebtoken.

findings.title: Unhandled exception in parseSession on malformed input
findings.body: parseSession passes the raw parameter directly into JSON.parse without error handling. Invalid JSON or undefined/non-string inputs will throw an unhandled SyntaxError/TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch block and validate the parsed object before returning userId.

samples.summary: The authentication module contains critical SQL injection, missing module dependencies, hardcoded secrets, and unhandled runtime exceptions.

findings.title: SQL injection in user lookup query
findings.body: In findUser, username is directly concatenated into the SQL query string without parameterization or escaping. This allows attackers to manipulate the SQL statement, bypass authentication, and access unauthorized data.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g., db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])).

findings.title: Missing ./db module dependency
findings.body: src/auth.js requires './db', but no corresponding db.js file exists in the repository, resulting in a MODULE_NOT_FOUND error when the module is imported.
findings.recommendation: Provide the missing ./db module and configure a package.json declaring jsonwebtoken and other dependencies.

findings.title: Unchecked user lookup result causes TypeError
findings.body: In login, if findUser returns null or undefined when a user is not found, evaluating user.password throws an unhandled TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Verify that user exists before checking credentials (e.g., if (user && user.password === password)).

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret and plaintext password verification
findings.body: The JWT signing secret is hardcoded directly in source code, and passwords are authenticated via plain equality comparison rather than using a secure cryptographic hashing function like bcrypt.
findings.recommendation: Load secrets from environment variables (process.env.JWT_SECRET) and use a secure hashing algorithm (such as bcrypt) for password verification.

findings.title: Unhandled JSON.parse exception on malformed input
findings.body: parseSession calls JSON.parse on raw input without error handling, which will throw an unhandled SyntaxError and crash the caller on malformed strings.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try-catch block and return null or handle malformed input gracefully.
